case_title: Surender Kaushik and Others v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others
neutral_facts: The case involves multiple FIRs registered against different accused persons for alleged forgery and fabrication of documents related to meetings of a society. The first FIR was lodged by an individual alleging that certain members of the society had prepared fake documents. A second FIR was registered based on a direction from a magistrate, alleging that the accused had fabricated documents and filed them with a competent authority. The allegations in the second FIR were distinct and separate from the first, involving different accused persons and different versions of the incident. The court held that the second FIR was permissible as it did not constitute an improvement of the facts in the first FIR and that the allegations were distinct and separate, thus not falling under the principle of sameness.
